definition: a person or company that owns a property and rents it out to others

collocations.example: A large corporate landlord now owns our apartment building.
The absentee landlord rarely visits or repairs the property.

definition: one complete trip around a track or course in a race

collocations.example: He fell behind on the last lap of the race.
Her lap time improved after weeks of hard training.

definition: a device that produces a narrow, very strong beam of light

collocations.example: The laser beam cut cleanly through the metal sheet.
Our office bought a fast new laser printer yesterday.

definition: clothes and sheets that need washing, or the act of washing them

collocations.example: The hotel offers a same-day laundry service for guests.
I need to do the laundry before the weekend.

definition: a flat, usually green part of a plant that grows from a stem

collocations.example: A red maple leaf fell slowly onto the path.
She read the pattern left by each tea leaf.

definition: something, such as money or an effect, passed on from the past or from someone

collocations.example: The retiring coach left a legacy of discipline and teamwork.
The leader left a lasting legacy of social reform.

definition: the group of people in a country or state who have the power to make laws

collocations.example: The state legislature passed the new tax law today.
That country has a unicameral legislature with one chamber.

definition: free time when you can relax and do what you enjoy

collocations.example: She spends her leisure time painting and reading books.
The leisure industry grew quickly along the coast.

definition: a yellow citrus fruit with a sour taste

collocations.example: Add fresh lemon juice to brighten the fish dish.
A lemon tree grew beside their kitchen window.

definition: a curved piece of glass or plastic that focuses light, as in a camera or glasses

collocations.example: He wiped the dusty camera lens with a soft cloth.
She lost a contact lens on the bathroom floor.

definition: relating to a woman who is sexually attracted to other women

collocations.example: The lesbian couple adopted two children last year.
The group campaigns for gay and lesbian rights.

definition: a bar or handle that you pull or push to operate a machine

collocations.example: He squeezed the brake lever to slow the bicycle.
She moved the gear lever into reverse carefully.

definition: to move your tongue across the surface of something

collocations.example: The child wanted to lick the spoon after baking.
The hungry dog licked its lips after the meal.

definition: an officer of middle rank in the army, navy, or police

collocations.example: The lieutenant colonel inspected the troops at dawn.
He was promoted to second lieutenant after training.

definition: in the same way; also

collocations.example: He recycles everything and urges his neighbors to do likewise.
The flood hit our town, and nearby villages were likewise affected.

definition: an arm or a leg of a person or animal

collocations.example: The accident caused a serious injury to his lower limb.
Physical therapy restored strength in her upper limb.

definition: arranged in a straight line, or changing at a constant rate

collocations.example: The graph shows a clear linear relationship between the variables.
Students learned to solve a simple linear equation.

definition: to stay somewhere or continue for longer than expected

collocations.example: The smell of smoke lingered on for hours.
They lingered over coffee long after dinner ended.

definition: relating to language or the study of language

collocations.example: Her linguistic competence impressed the interview panel greatly.
The paper offers a detailed linguistic analyzis of regional dialects.

definition: the ability to read and write

collocations.example: The program helps adults improve their literacy skills.
She volunteers at an adult literacy center downtown.

definition: full of energy, interest, and enthusiasm

collocations.example: Her lively personality made the whole office feel cheerful.
The proposal sparked a lively debate among the members.

definition: a large organ in the body that cleans the blood

collocations.example: Heavy drinking can cause serious liver damage over time.
The blood test checked his liver function carefully.

definition: a strong feeling of wanting something or someone

collocations.example: She felt a deep longing for her childhood home.
His letters revealed a deep longing to return.

definition: to appear large or threatening, or to be about to happen

collocations.example: Financial worries loomed large in their minds.
Serious problems loomed ahead for the struggling company.

definition: a shape made by a line or rope that curves round and crosses itself

collocations.example: The wire forms a closed loop around the magnet.
She tied the rope into a small loop.

definition: a comfortable room for sitting and relaxing, as in a hotel or airport

collocations.example: Passengers waited in the departure lounge before boarding.
They met for drinks in the hotel cocktail lounge.

definition: one of the two organs in the chest used for breathing

collocations.example: Years of heavy smoking led to his lung cancer.
Regular swimming can increase your lung capacity.

definition: the words of a song

collocations.example: He quoted a famous song lyric in his speech.
She can write a catchy lyric in minutes.

definition: extremely beautiful or impressive

collocations.example: From the hilltop we enjoyed a magnificent view.
The museum is a truly magnificent building.

definition: the great size or importance of something

collocations.example: No one grasped the sheer magnitude of the disaster.
Few understood the magnitude of the problem they faced.

definition: a warm-blooded animal that feeds its young with milk

collocations.example: The whale is the largest marine mammal alive.
A bat is a small warm-blooded mammal that flies.

definition: the authority given to an elected government or person to act

collocations.example: The election gave the party a clear mandate.
The new president claimed a strong popular mandate to reform.

definition: a written or typed version of a book before it is printed

collocations.example: The original manuscript was lost during the war.
She will submit her manuscript to the publisher soon.

definition: a hard stone used for buildings and statues

collocations.example: Her heels clicked across the polished marble floor.
A white marble statue stood in the garden.

definition: walked with regular steps, especially as a group or soldiers

collocations.example: Thousands of protesters marched through the city center.
The soldiers marched on toward the distant border.

definition: a small piece of material placed on the floor for a purpose

collocations.example: Wipe your shoes on the door mat please.
She stepped onto the soft bath mat.

definition: an arrangement of numbers in rows and columns

collocations.example: The student calculated the inverse matrix by hand.
The engineers stored the data as a sparse matrix.

definition: to make something as great or large as possible

collocations.example: The firm cut costs to maximise profits.
They aimed to maximise the value of each asset.

definition: the period of time between two events

collocations.example: Dinner is almost ready; set the table in the meantime.
For the meantime, just keep the old system running.

definition: a flat piece of metal given as an award for an achievement

collocations.example: She won the gold medal in the swimming final.
He settled for the silver medal this time.

definition: to help two sides in a disagreement reach an agreement

collocations.example: A neutral lawyer was asked to mediate the dispute.
She tried to mediate between the two angry parties.

definition: relating to the Middle Ages, roughly from 1000 to 1500

collocations.example: They explored a ruined medieval castle on the hill.
He teaches medieval history at the university.

definition: a series of musical notes that make a tune

collocations.example: The song has a simple, catchy melody.
She can play a melody by ear quite easily.

definition: a person who buys and sells goods, especially in large amounts

collocations.example: Her grandfather was a respected wine merchant in town.
A wealthy merchant funded the town's new harbor.

definition: kindness shown by not punishing someone you have power over

collocations.example: The judge chose to show mercy to the young offender.
The prisoners begged for mercy from their captors.

definition: the quality of being good and deserving praise or reward

collocations.example: The film has little artistic merit despite its budget.
Each application is judged on merit alone.

definition: a way of describing something by calling it something else

collocations.example: The poet uses a metaphor to describe her grief.
A river is an apt metaphor for the passing of time.

definition: relating to a large city and the area around it

collocations.example: The metropolitan area has over five million residents.
The metropolitan police increased patrols downtown.

definition: very strong, large, or powerful

collocations.example: The mighty river carved through the deep canyon.
The mighty empire ruled for over three centuries.

definition: ready to use strong or aggressive action to support a cause

collocations.example: The militant group claimed responsibility for the attack.
The union took a militant stance in the negotiations.

definition: a unit of weight equal to one thousandth of a gram

collocations.example: A single milligram of the substance proved harmful.
The dose was five milligrams per kilogram of body weight.

definition: a natural substance found in the ground, such as metal or salt

collocations.example: The company discovered a rich mineral deposit underground.
The region is famous for its mineral resources.

definition: very small in amount; as little as possible

collocations.example: The repair was done at minimal cost.
He passed the exam with minimal effort.

definition: to reduce something to the smallest possible amount

collocations.example: Safety training helps minimise the risk of accidents.
The factory redesigned its process to minimise waste.

definition: a very lucky or wonderful event that seems impossible

collocations.example: The country's rapid growth was called an economic miracle.
The doctors could not work a miracle for him.

definition: very unhappy or uncomfortable

collocations.example: She felt miserable after losing her job.
We endured cold, miserable weather all week.

definition: a thin cloud of tiny water drops in the air near the ground

collocations.example: A thick morning mist covered the quiet valley.
The ship appeared slowly through the mist.

definition: to organize people or resources so they are ready for a purpose

collocations.example: The campaign worked hard to mobilise public support.
The agency moved quickly to mobilise relief resources.

definition: not real; done as practice or for pretend

collocations.example: Students took a mock exam before the real test.
The career center offers a mock interview service.

definition: very small amounts of water in the air or on a surface

collocations.example: The machine measures the moisture content of the grain.
Good soil helps plants retain moisture for longer.

definition: the force that keeps something moving or developing

collocations.example: The campaign began to gain momentum last month.
The project started to lose momentum after the delays.

definition: a king or queen who rules a country

collocations.example: The reigning monarch opened the new parliament today.
Britain has a constitutional monarch with limited power.

definition: relating to money or a country's supply of money

collocations.example: The central bank tightened its monetary policy.
The old painting has great monetary value today.

definition: complete control of a product or service by one company

collocations.example: The water supply is often a natural monopoly.
Regulators worried about the firm's growing monopoly power.

definition: a structure built to remember a person or event

collocations.example: The old fort is now a national monument.
Tourists photographed the famous historic monument.

definition: a hollow container that gives shape to liquid or soft material as it hardens

collocations.example: The molten metal was poured into the mould.
A clay mould is used to cast the bronze statue.

definition: to feel or show great sadness, especially when someone dies

collocations.example: The whole village mourned for the lost sailors.
They gathered to mourn the death of their leader.

definition: a title used before a woman's family name, without showing if she is married

collocations.example: Ms Smith will chair the meeting this afternoon.
She prefers to be addressed as Ms rather than Mrs.

definition: to add a number to itself a particular number of times

collocations.example: Multiply the length by the width to get the area.
Children learn to multiply two numbers at school.

definition: relating to a town or city and its local government

collocations.example: The municipal government approved the new budget.
The municipal council meets every second Tuesday.

definition: a soft, low sound, or words spoken very quietly

collocations.example: A low murmur of voices filled the hall.
Her speech drew a murmur of approval from the crowd.

definition: a fungus with a stem and a rounded top, often eaten as food

collocations.example: She ordered a bowl of creamy mushroom soup.
The recipe calls for a handful of button mushrooms.

definition: to speak quietly and unclearly, often when annoyed

collocations.example: He muttered under his breath about the long delay.
She muttered a reply and walked away quickly.

definition: to find the way to a place, especially by ship, plane, or car

collocations.example: Early sailors learned to navigate by the stars.
The captain had to navigate the ship through fog.

definition: something that you must have or that is necessary

collocations.example: Clean water is a basic necessity of life.
She took the job out of necessity, not choice.

definition: a thin, pointed metal tool used for sewing

collocations.example: She threaded the sewing needle with red cotton.
It is hard to thread the needle in dim light.

definition: a very frightening or unpleasant experience

collocations.example: Their dream holiday turned into a nightmare.
The long legal battle became a living nightmare.

definition: having or showing fine personal qualities such as honesty and courage

collocations.example: The volunteers worked hard for a noble cause.
Despite his noble intentions, the plan still failed.

definition: in spite of what has just been said; however

collocations.example: The detail is small but nonetheless important.
The risks remain nonetheless, despite the new safeguards.

definition: words or ideas that are silly or make no sense

collocations.example: Stop talking nonsense and listen to me.
His excuse was sheer nonsense from start to finish.

definition: twelve o'clock in the middle of the day

collocations.example: The meeting will start at noon sharp.
We should reach the summit by noon.

definition: a standard or usual way of behaving

collocations.example: Shaking hands is a common social norm here.
They treat punctuality as an important cultural norm.

definition: well known for something bad

collocations.example: The road is notorious for serious accidents.
Police finally caught the notorious criminal.

definition: a place where young children are cared for while parents work

collocations.example: Her young son attends a nearby nursery school.
She leaves her baby at a day nursery each morning.

definition: the process of getting the right food for good health

collocations.example: Good nutrition is essential for healthy growth.
She checked the nutrition facts on the label.

definition: to do what you are told or what a rule says

collocations.example: All players must obey the rules of the game.
Soldiers are trained to obey orders without question.

definition: not well known, or difficult to understand

collocations.example: The essay was full of obscure references.
The writer remained relatively obscure during her life.

definition: to think about something so much that you cannot think of anything else

collocations.example: Good editors obsess over small details in every sentence.
Try not to obsess about the future so much.

definition: something that makes it difficult to achieve something

collocations.example: Lack of funding is the major obstacle to the plan.
The team worked hard to overcome every obstacle.

definition: to block something or get in the way of its progress

collocations.example: They were charged with trying to obstruct justice.
A tall fence obstructed the view of the sea.

definition: a smell, especially one that is unpleasant

collocations.example: An offensive odor came from the blocked drain.
The empty room had a stale odor.

definition: to balance the effect of something, making it smaller

collocations.example: Higher sales helped offset the rising cost of materials.
New customers offset the loss of the old ones.

definition: a small green or black fruit used for food and oil

collocations.example: She drizzled olive oil over the fresh salad.
An old olive tree stood in the quiet courtyard.

definition: to leave something out and not include it

collocations.example: Be careful not to omit a word when copying.

definition: continuing to happen or develop

collocations.example: Learning a language is an ongoing process.

definition: to treat people in a cruel and unfair way, limiting their freedom

collocations.example: The harsh laws oppress the poor most of all.

definition: to choose one thing rather than another

collocations.example: Many travelers opt for cheaper night flights.

definition: relating to the eye or to sight

collocations.example: The optic nerve carries signals from the eye.
The doctor examined the optic disc during the eye test.

definition: a person who always expects good things to happen

collocations.example: She is an incurable optimist about almost everything.
He is a born optimist who never gives up.
